targetText:
The victory of the Cuban Revolution will be a tangible
demonstration before all the Americas that peoples are capable of
rising up, that they can rise up by themselves right under the very
fangs of the monster. It will mean the beginning of the end of
colonial domination in America, that is, the definitive beginning of
the end for North American imperialism.
explanation: Che identifies the global historical significance of Cuba: breaking the myth of imperialist invulnerability across Latin America and demonstrating that dependent nations can liberate themselves through organized struggle.

targetText:
The murder of Patrice Lumumba is an example of what the
empire is capable of when the struggle against it is carried on in a
firm and sustained way. Imperialism must be struck on the snout
once, and again, and then again, in an infinite succession of blows
and counter-blows. That is the only way the people can win their
real independence.
explanation: Che draws internationalist lessons from the assassination of anti-colonial leaders, insisting that compromising with imperialist powers results in disaster; liberation demands unrelenting counter-attacks.
context: Patrice Lumumba, the first democratically elected Prime Minister of the Republic of the Congo, was murdered in January 1961 in a plot backed by Belgian and US intelligence agencies. Che frequently pointed to Lumumba's assassination as historical proof that imperialism never grants genuine sovereignty voluntarily.

targetText:
Cuba's victory lies not in Soviet rockets, nor in the
solidarity of the socialist world, nor in the solidarity of the whole
world. Cuba's victory lies in the unity, the labour, and the spirit
of sacrifice of its people.
explanation: While appreciating Soviet and internationalist solidarity, Che emphasizes self-reliance: external support cannot replace domestic class unity, disciplined production, and mass commitment to defense.
